title: Set up reproducible screenshot pipeline
body:
Two-tier approach from June 2026 research:
- Inline circuit shots: keep each circuit as a .litematic in git (doubles as downloadable course asset); render with the Isometric Renders mod (/isorender area) for transparent-background orthographic PNGs. Technical Utilities mod can render the current Litematica selection directly.
- Hero/chapter shots: Chunky headless. One scene.json per shot committed to git (camera/FOV/chunks); re-shoot after world edits with: chunky -render <scene> -f -reload-chunks.
- Shared post-process script: magick mogrify -trim, pad to consistent aspect, oxipng/pngquant.
Links: https://modrinth.com/mod/isometric-renders https://github.com/chunky-dev/chunky https://modrinth.com/mod/techutils

title: Resolve architecture.md open questions (13) against in-world build
body: architecture.md section 11 lists 13 decisions. Critical ones: #5 flag-latch timing vs Reg A load (countdown loop correctness), #1 IR/AR never built, #2 Reg B never built, #3 selector encodings. Verify/correct architecture.md from the real machine first, then conform the 12a/12b drafts to it. Blocks line-editing Part III.

title: Repo hygiene: stray files and duplicate images
body:
- pi-session-2026-03-17*.html (2.8 MB) at repo root looks accidentally committed
- .DS_Store files committed in several dirs (add to .gitignore)
- 3 byte-identical duplicate images: AND-gate-composite_minecraft.png + XOR-gate-composite_minecraft.png (03b dup of 03), digital-display-subcircuit-abstractions_circuitverse.png (04b dup of 04)

Bedrock update: Litematica/Isometric Renders/Chunky are all Java-only. But MiEx (bramstout/MiEx) reads BEDROCK worlds natively (1.17+), runs on macOS (Java jar), has a -cli headless mode, exports USD -> Blender Cycles. Studio-grade quality (used for Minecraft Live). Likely unified pipeline: Bedrock world -> MiEx -> Blender with two camera templates (orthographic diagram / cinematic hero), headless via blender -b. Fallback/alt: Chunker CLI (HiveGamesOSS, MIT, headless) converts Bedrock->Java scriptably for any Java-only tool; redstone block states survive conversion (spot-check first run). Avoyd is Windows-only (dead end). Vibrant Visuals shots only possible on an actual Bedrock device, no macOS client.
Links: https://github.com/BramStoutProductions/MiEx https://github.com/HiveGamesOSS/Chunker https://github.com/Moo-Ack-Productions/MCprep https://github.com/Moulberry/Flashback

Revised architecture idea from Fielding: Java server (Fabric) + Geyser/Floodgate, Bedrock world converted once via Chunker. Unlocks: no recurring conversion (Chunky/MiEx read server world dir directly), server-side .schem export via WorldEdit/FAWE (no Java client needed), Carpet+scarpet for automated truth-table verification of circuits + /tick freeze for staging, BlueMap for embeddable interactive 3D views in the Astro site, multiplayer. Caveat: Java server = Java redstone mechanics through the Bedrock client; keep original Bedrock world as Bedrock-mechanics test bed; verify each converted circuit (esp. timing-sensitive Part III builds).

title: Set up reproducible screenshot pipeline
body:
Two-tier approach from June 2026 research:
- Inline circuit shots: keep each circuit as a .litematic in git (doubles as downloadable course asset); render with the Isometric Renders mod (/isorender area) for transparent-background orthographic PNGs. Technical Utilities mod can render the current Litematica selection directly.
- Hero/chapter shots: Chunky headless. One scene.json per shot committed to git (camera/FOV/chunks); re-shoot after world edits with: chunky -render <scene> -f -reload-chunks.
- Shared post-process script: magick mogrify -trim, pad to consistent aspect, oxipng/pngquant.
Links: https://modrinth.com/mod/isometric-renders https://github.com/chunky-dev/chunky https://modrinth.com/mod/techutils

Pipeline is live end-to-end: Bedrock world -> MiEx (worlds via miex.env MIEX_ADDITIONAL_SAVE_DIRS; vanilla assets extracted from Mojang client jars in ~/Library/Application Support/minecraft/versions) -> USD -> scripts/render_usd.py (headless Blender 5.1, Cycles/Metal, auto-fit iso+beauty cameras, Closest texture filtering). Usage: blender -b -P scripts/render_usd.py -- file.usd [--views iso,beauty --res WxH --samples N --out DIR --azimuth DEG]. Verified on real build export (259 objects, ~90s for both views at 1920x1440). Remaining: tight-Y export discipline, per-module scene/region presets in MiEx, post-process trim/pad step, decide where renders land in src/*/images.

Headless pipeline COMPLETE: renders/shots.json (per-circuit world+bounds+views config, in git) -> scripts/shots.py -> MiEx -cli (loadWorld/setActiveResourcePacks/applyExportSettings/export commands) -> scripts/render_usd.py -> PNGs. Verified on 7segment. REQUIRED LOCAL PATCH: MiEx exp-23 applyExportSettings has 2 bugs (ExportData.fromJson passes parent JSON to ExportBounds.fromJson instead of entry2; reflection checks Integer/Float/Boolean.isAssignableFrom which never match primitive int/float/boolean fields) - patched classes compiled and jar-updated, stock backup at ~/apps/MiEx/MiEx.jar.orig. Candidate upstream PR. Caveats: MiEx GUI must be closed (LevelDB lock, shots.py checks), Bedrock saves only on world exit (shots.py errors on empty exports).

Renderer feature-complete for course use: --dust solid|power|schematic|realistic (solid default: clean geometric strokes from generated textures in renders/assets/, state-colored shadeless emission, powered glows); --swap old=new block retexturing at render time; --lighting/--transform/--glare/--elevation overrides; scripts/sweep.py style+angle contact sheets. renders/STYLE.md is the style standard (lane color palette TODO for Fielding). Verified on big.usd lab render. Next: angle-sweep Part I builds, fill shots.json, regenerate course images, COMMIT EVERYTHING.

title: Schematic-symbol overlay on CAD aerial render (Tier 1)
body:
Idea from render exploration. The CAD aerial (--technical cad on top view) reads like a PCB layout and is genuinely useful. Next level: overlay standard logic/EE glyphs at component positions, keeping real spatial layout + the extracted dust wire graph:
- redstone torch -> NOT gate (triangle + bubble)
- repeater -> delay/buffer box (show delay ticks)
- comparator -> comparator symbol
- wire tees -> junction dots
We already have component positions (materials) and the wire connection graph (build_vector_wires). Work is drawing/placing glyphs (Blender geometry at world positions facing camera, or PIL compositing at projected screen coords). Solves the 'need a key' problem since symbols are self-explanatory.

NOT doing: Tier 2 (full netlist extraction + re-layout into idealized left-to-right schematic). That's an EDA-grade auto-placement problem; for a course, hand-drawn schematics or the existing Boolean expressions are clearer, and re-layout breaks the spatial correspondence to the build that makes the overlay pedagogically useful.

title: Unified design system across site + Blender schematics + CircuitVerse
body:
Lock ONE visual language across three surfaces so figures and chrome feel consistent.

Canonical palette (single source of truth) drives all three:
- Signal ON = redstone red (site --color-primary oklch(48% 0.18 25)); physically correct AND on-brand. REPLACES CircuitVerse's current lime-green=on.
- Signal OFF = warm grey.
- Accent / logic gates = amber-gold (site --color-accent oklch(78% 0.14 70)); CircuitVerse orange gates already close.
- Backgrounds: warm near-black (dark) / warm paper (light); structure neutrals from site greys.
- Layer height tints (Minecraft renders only): muted earthy per-layer hues, light+dark matched.

Apply to:
1. Site: web/src/styles/global.css :root tokens (currently dark-only, single :root). Fielding leaning toward RESKINNING site to fit the schematics rather than vice versa. Decide dark-only vs light-mode vs light-entirely.
2. Blender renders: scripts/render_usd.py TECHNICAL palettes (already parameterized; mostly done).
3. CircuitVerse: configure a Custom Theme (wire on=red, off=grey, gate=gold, bg) and use for all future captures; re-capture existing *_circuitverse.png for consistency. CircuitVerse supports custom themes (UI theme editor).

KEY semantic decision: ON=red everywhere (kill green=on in CircuitVerse). The green/red conflict is the biggest current inconsistency.
Down-the-road effort; foundation step = author the canonical palette/tokens doc that all three reference.

title: Automate CircuitVerse SVG cleanup (replace manual Figma step)
body: Current workflow: export SVG from CircuitVerse -> hand-clean in Figma (significant time per diagram). Automate: programmatic SVG transform applying the locked design system (recolor wires on=red/off=grey, gates=gold, bg, strip/normalize, consistent sizing). Likely an SVG-processing script (svgo + recolor map, or lxml). Depends on canonical palette (ru-7093b6).

title: Place Minecraft renders into the course
body:
Full render pass is DONE — 34 shots rendered to renders/out/ (iso + top, ground-removed, new schematic style; 0 black/empty). They are NOT yet placed into src/.../images/. This is the next big task.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Map each shot's iso render -> its course filename. Convention: strip the NN_/NNb_ module prefix, append _minecraft.png. e.g. 04_2-to-4-decoder-2_iso.png -> src/Part-I--Foundations/04_Decoders-and-Displays/images/2-to-4-decoder-2_minecraft.png. Use scripts/publish.py optimize_and_copy_image(src,dst) (1600px + pngquant) like prior placements.
2. Naming fixes: shot 04_complete-digital-display -> complete-digital-display_minecraft.png (dash). The old 7segment shot is superseded; the real 7-seg figure is COMPOSED (see 4).
3. iso+aerial PAIRING: for decoders/displays/encoders (anything from decoders on up), place BOTH the iso AND the top view, paired side-by-side. Pairing mechanism already built: two consecutive image lines in the SAME paragraph in the draft -> CSS .prose p:has(img+img) lays them in a flex row (see web/src/pages/course/[...slug].astro). Aerial filename convention: <base>-aerial_minecraft.png (the _top render). GATES (NOT/OR/AND/NOR/gate composites, powered blocks, basic-circuit, input) get ISO ONLY (no aerial) per user.
4. 7-SEGMENT composite: 7-segment-display_minecraft.png is a 4-stage figure composed left-to-right from shots 7-segment-a, -b, -c, -d (iso renders). Compose them horizontally on transparent bg (like the original assets/images/04_7-segment-display_minecraft.png) and place as src/Part-I--Foundations/04_Decoders-and-Displays/images/7-segment-display_minecraft.png.
5. Adding aerials = NEW images -> edit the source draft.md (in src/, NOT web/) to add the second image line. Content edits go through src per user.
6. After placing: cd web && node scripts/sync-content.mjs. Dev image cache is fixed (no-store), so refresh shows immediately.

Earlier session already placed the Module 4 decoder set (ground-KEPT, older style) — those need replacing with the new ground-removed renders + aerials.
